brief:
Gadi Eisenkot, a former general positioning himself as the antithesis to Benjamin Netanyahu, has emerged as a leading opposition figure in Israeli politics, The Guardian reported. Described as "menschy" and unpolished compared to the prime minister, Eisenkot contrasts with Netanyahu's style and character while maintaining studied ambiguity on key policy questions including peace efforts.

The candidate's appeal rests partly on personal presentation—casting himself as straightforward where Netanyahu appears calculated. Yet Eisenkot has avoided taking clear stances on several fundamental issues that will define Israel's political future, raising questions about what his leadership would substantively offer beyond opposition to the current premier.
dek: The ‘menschy’ former general contrasts with the current PM when it comes to style and character – yet on key policy points retains a studied ambiguity He has been called the man who is everything the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is not.
title: Israeli opposition candidate Eisenkot offers style contrast, policy ambiguity on Netanyahu
